Tl-DW - A light sensor measures the coin, then electromagnets detect the material.

I suppose this means if you made copper slugs the same size as quarters it would probably work (might have to taint them with some nickel). Might end up costing more than the quarter though.

EDIT: Just for fun, here's the math.

A quarter weighs about 5.6 grams. It is made up of about 91% copper. A gram of 100% pure copper goes for about half a cent, so 5.1 grams, or a quarter's worth, would cost you a little over 2 and a half cents. Now, if pure copper will work, then you can basically make quarters for literally 10% of the cost, assuming you have the capability to shape them into slugs yourself. If you have to taint the copper with Nickel, it gets a little more expensive, but not by much. Pure Nickel goes for about $7.70 for 100G, so about 8 cents a gram. You'd need about half a gram per quarter, so you'd be adding about 4 cents to your cost, which means you could still be making quarters for about 6 and a half cents a pop.

Not bad. If you are already good at metal working you could basically never pay for soda again.
